findings.finding: The rename of `completion_verifier.md:59`'s Epic section heading from `## Success Criteria` to `## Acceptance Criteria` changes what the verifier prompt expects from plans, but the plan does not mention checking for or updating any author-facing plan template, contributor guide, or AGENTS.md that may instruct authors to write a `## Success Criteria` heading — leaving those references stale and silently breaking completion verification for in-flight plans authored under the old convention.
scenarios: An author writes a new plan with `## Success Criteria` (following an un-updated template or guide); the renamed verifier prompt no longer recognises the heading, producing a spurious incomplete-plan verdict
A reviewer of the stale template file sees 'Success Criteria' and assumes it is still valid, propagating the old convention
findings.suggested_fix: Search the repo for `## Success Criteria` outside the already-enumerated paths (e.g. `grep -rn '## Success Criteria' docs/ AGENTS.md .github/ templates/`) and either add any hits to the Scope list or explicitly record their absence as a confirmed non-issue in the plan.

findings.finding: src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md (lines 58, 76) is an unenumerated consumer that uses the exact 'Success Criteria' heading vocabulary being renamed. It is the canonical author guide served live via `rebar explain plan` and the MCP `explain_criterion` tool, and it explicitly tells ticket authors to write `## Success Criteria` for container tickets. The plan's AC grep is path-scoped to `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/` and `criteria_routing.json`, so this file is invisible to the check. After the rename, reviewer rubrics say 'Acceptance Criteria' while this guide still directs authors to produce `## Success Criteria` — a contradictory vocabulary that defeats the stated goal.
scenarios: A ticket author reads `rebar explain plan` after this story lands and follows its instruction to write `## Success Criteria`; the renamed reviewer rubrics (G3, G7, container) now call the same concept 'Acceptance Criteria', creating a terminology inconsistency the rubrics were designed to eliminate.
The E1 criterion (terminology consistency) may fire on tickets whose authors followed the guide's `## Success Criteria` instruction while the rubric now expects `## Acceptance Criteria`.

T4 requires the remedy to be an explicit rollback or expand-contract — sequencing alone satisfies the 'land in right order' constraint, but does not address 'what if we need to undo this after it lands'.

findings.finding: `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:317` synthesizes epic ticket descriptions that include a `## Success Criteria` heading in live eval code (not archived data). The plan names `completion_verifier.md:59` for editing — that line tells the verifier to recognise `## Success Criteria` in Epics. If that recogniser is renamed to `## Acceptance Criteria`, the eval solver's synthetic epics (which still carry `## Success Criteria`) will no longer be recognised by the updated verifier, silently breaking coverage for those eval cases. This file is not named in the plan's Scope and is outside the AC grep path.
scenarios: After completion_verifier.md:59 is renamed to `## Acceptance Criteria`, the verifier stops looking for `## Success Criteria` in epics. The eval solver still generates synthetic epics with `## Success Criteria` headings. Eval runs may under-count criteria, producing misleading fidelity scores.

If actual legacy epic tickets in the live system still carry `## Success Criteria` headings (they were authored against the old guide), removing this recogniser from completion_verifier.md silently drops those criteria from completion verification.
